audit_metadata.scope: Domain intent separation, observation dedup, agro report lote resolution

pipeline_order: 1. Trivial command bypass (confirm, cancel, greeting, help, menu, etc.) → confidence 0.95
2. Full regex chain: commands → income → expense → partial → observation bypass → financial guard → general observation → bare reference → unknown
3. AI threshold check: if regex confidence ≥ 0.75, skip AI entirely
4. AI extraction (Claude Haiku) for low-confidence results

observation_prefix_detection.behavior: Anchored to start of string. Matches 'observación:', 'obs:', 'nota -', etc.
observation_prefix_detection.bypass_effect: When matched, routes DIRECTLY to log_observation at confidence 0.95, bypassing hasAgroActivity guard entirely
observation_prefix_detection.example_observacion_riego_en_lote_1: With prefix → routed as log_observation (0.95). Without prefix → hasAgroActivity matches 'riego', observation parser skipped, falls to bare reference (0.70), then AI extractor handles structured irrigation extraction

agro_activity_guard.effect: When matched AND no observation prefix, blocks parsearObservacion to let AI handle structured activity extraction

financial_intent_guard.runs_at: Step 2.6 — after observation bypass but before general observation
financial_intent_guard.behavior: If financial keyword found + amount extractable → routes to expense (0.85) or expense_partial (0.60)

agro_report_patterns.extract_logic: Checks if matched string m[0] contains 'lote' → returns plotName; otherwise → returns fieldName
agro_report_patterns.known_gap: 'reporte lote 1' (without 'agronómico' or 'semanal') matches plot_report, NOT generate_agro_report. This is by design.

edge_case_observacion_financial.result: CORRECTLY intercepted as expense at step 2.3 (expense parser runs before observation bypass at step 2.5). Pipeline ordering provides natural protection.

layers.logic: Requires BOTH a financial verb AND an amount pattern. Returns null if matched.
layers.verdict: CORRECT — dual-signal requirement prevents false positives

layers.logic: Map<string, timestamp> with key 'userId:plotId:normalizedText'. TTL: 5 minutes. Pruned lazily on each saveObservation call.
layers.verdict: CORRECT dedup logic, BUT null return causes misleading UX (see bugs)

layers.sql: SELECT id FROM agro_observations WHERE user_id=$1 AND normalized_text=$2 AND COALESCE(plot_id,0)=COALESCE($3,0) AND created_at > NOW()-INTERVAL '5 minutes'
layers.index: idx_agro_obs_dedup on (user_id, COALESCE(plot_id,0), normalized_text, created_at DESC)
layers.verdict: CORRECT dedup logic, BUT truthy return causes false success confirmation (see bugs)

layers.logic: deduplicateObservations() — Set-based dedup by 'plotId:normalizedText', keeps first occurrence

steps: Strip 'en [el] lote/campo X...' and everything after
normalization.verdict: CORRECT — handles case, accents, punctuation, location suffixes

text_cleaning.observation_prefix_stripped: YES — parsearObservacion strips 'lote X' and 'campo X' references from observationText
text_cleaning.raw_text_stored: observation_text column stores the text passed to saveObservation (from parser, not raw user message)
text_cleaning.normalized_text_stored: normalized_text column stores the normalized version for dedup queries

financial_leakage_into_reports.evidence: No query in observations.js, agronomy.handler.ts, or agro-report.js references expenses or incomes tables. Domain events table (domain_events) is separate agronomic-only table.

report_title_consistency.detail: When user asks 'reporte agronómico lote 1', the title reads 'Reporte agronómico — [Campo Name]' (parent campo), NOT 'lote 1'. Data IS correctly scoped to lote 1, but title references parent campo.

phrasing_consistency.reporte_lote_1_without_agronomico: → plot_report (DIFFERENT handler — by design, see known_gap)
phrasing_consistency.reporte_campo_norte_without_agronomico: → generate_agro_report (pattern #5 catches 'reporte + campo') — slight inconsistency with lote variant

pdf_vs_text_scoping.detail: generateWeeklyReport(userId, field.id) creates a FIELD-scoped PDF (all lotes), but the WhatsApp text message is correctly LOTE-scoped. User receives narrowly-scoped text + broadly-scoped PDF.

observation_isolation.verdict: STRICT — lote 2 observations cannot appear in lote 1 reports

activity_isolation.method: User-wide DB fetch (last 10 events) + JS filter by plotIds Set
activity_isolation.verdict: SAFE but slightly inefficient — if user's last 10 events are all on other lotes, target lote shows 0 activities even if it has older ones

plot_discovery_safety.detail: Handler checks resolved.autoCreated — refuses to generate reports for auto-created (non-existent) lotes

financial_to_agro.pipeline_guard: Expense parser (step 2.3) runs BEFORE observation bypass (step 2.5) — financial messages intercepted first
financial_to_agro.storage_guard: hasFinancialContent() in saveObservation rejects text with financial verb + amount pattern
financial_to_agro.report_guard: Agro report queries only agro_observations and domain_events tables — no joins to expenses/incomes
financial_to_agro.verdict: TRIPLE-LAYER PROTECTION — no contamination path found

agro_to_financial.detail: Financial queries (FinancialRepository, expenses.js) only touch expenses/incomes tables — no reference to agro_observations or domain_events

table_separation.verdict: Clean table-level separation — no cross-domain data mixing possible at SQL level

critical_bugs.title: In-memory dedup returns null → misleading 'looks like expense' message
critical_bugs.description: saveObservation returns null for BOTH financial guard rejection AND in-memory dedup rejection. The handler's if(!saved) check shows 'Eso parece un gasto o ingreso' for ALL null returns, including legitimate duplicate observations. User is told their crop observation looks like a financial transaction when it was actually rejected as a duplicate.
critical_bugs.impact: User confusion — correct observation rejected with wrong error message
critical_bugs.fix: Return distinct sentinel values from saveObservation (e.g., { rejected: 'financial' } vs { rejected: 'duplicate' }) or throw typed errors so handler can give appropriate feedback

critical_bugs.title: DB dedup returns existing row → false success confirmation
critical_bugs.description: When in-memory cache misses but DB dedup catches a duplicate, saveObservation returns the existing row's {id} (truthy). The handler treats this as a successful save and confirms to the user. The user sees 'observation saved' but nothing was actually inserted.
critical_bugs.impact: Minor UX issue — user sees confirmation for a no-op, but no data corruption occurs
critical_bugs.fix: Return a flag indicating whether the row was newly inserted or already existed

critical_bugs.title: Report title uses campo name, not lote name, for lote-scoped reports
critical_bugs.description: When user requests 'reporte agronómico lote 1', the WhatsApp message title and PDF caption say 'Reporte agronómico — [Campo Name]' instead of indicating the specific lote. Data is correctly scoped but title is misleading.
critical_bugs.impact: User may think the report covers the full campo when it only covers the requested lote

critical_bugs.title: PDF attachment is field-scoped while text message is lote-scoped
critical_bugs.description: generateWeeklyReport(userId, field.id) creates a PDF for the ENTIRE campo (all lotes), but the WhatsApp text summary correctly filters to the requested lote only. User receives a narrowly-scoped text summary contradicted by a broadly-scoped PDF.
critical_bugs.impact: Data inconsistency between text and PDF attachment

critical_bugs.title: Activity fetch is user-wide with hard LIMIT 10, then JS-filtered
critical_bugs.description: getDomainEventsByUser(userId, 10) fetches the last 10 events for the entire user, then filters in JS by plotIds. If the user's last 10 events are all on other lotes, the target lote shows 0 activities even if it has older ones.
critical_bugs.impact: Lote-scoped reports may undercount activities for less-active lotes

critical_bugs.title: 'reporte lote 1' routes to plot_report, 'reporte campo norte' routes to generate_agro_report
critical_bugs.description: Without the 'agronómico' keyword, 'reporte lote X' matches plot_report while 'reporte campo X' matches generate_agro_report (pattern #5). This asymmetry means lote and campo get different report types for the same shorthand phrasing.
critical_bugs.impact: User gets different report format depending on whether they reference lote or campo

insights: The bot has a well-layered architecture with strong domain separation. Financial and agronomic data are cleanly separated at the table level — no SQL query crosses domains. The observation deduplication system is robust with 4 layers (financial guard → in-memory cache → DB dedup → output dedup), and the normalization function handles case, accents, punctuation, and location suffixes correctly. Cross-lote isolation is enforced at the DB level with strict WHERE plot_id=$1 queries. The main issues are UX-level: (1) the handler cannot distinguish between financial rejection and dedup rejection (both return null), causing a misleading error message for duplicates; (2) the PDF attachment is field-scoped while the text summary is correctly lote-scoped, creating an inconsistency; (3) report titles reference the parent campo even for lote-scoped reports. No data corruption, no domain contamination, and no cross-lote leakage was found.
